title: Natty or not (.com): Omar Isuf
summary: He debunks a 2014 natty-or-not article accusing Omar Isuf of steroid use, arguing Omar's physique is ordinary and achievable by almost anyone who keeps training. Such articles lower natural standards, push unrealistic leanness, and poison beginners' belief in what is possible.
claims: Omar Isuf's physique is nothing special and achievable naturally by anyone who puts in time, effort and study; he feels the same about his own physique
Calling modest physiques unnatural tells beginners that even mediocre goals require steroids, which is harmful nonsense
Powerlifting standards rose so fast that Omar's lifts, elite for a natural in 2014, are mediocre seven years later; bodybuilding went the other way and natural physiques are degrading
175 cm at 82 kg raises no red flags at all; reaching 90 kg at that height would not be shocking either
Body fat skews the equation: the more muscle a natural builds, the more fat he can carry while still looking good, so he can get bigger overall
A 65 kg skinny guy aiming for 90 kg does not need 25 kg of dry muscle; a large share will be fat and water on top of muscle, and he will look bigger and better, not fatter
People on the internet underestimate body fat by about 5%; Omar sits around 15-16% outside aggressive cuts, not 10-12%
No natural can reach 5% body fat without looking like a skeleton; chasing pro bodybuilder leanness is an illusion for naturals
Natty-or-not crusaders hunt witches while promoting diets and training standards that only enhanced people can reach, leaving naturals in terrible shape
Natural bodybuilding competitions demanding extreme dryness are not natural bodybuilding, just a drug-free copy of another sport
Developed delts, big rear delts, upper chest striations or traps are not signs of steroids; naturals can develop any muscle, it is just harder
Natty-or-not content harms viewers more than creators: believing your idols are enhanced convinces you that you cannot reach their level and lowers your standards
Only a minority of people could not reach Omar's (or his) level of muscle naturally if they never stop lifting
Most natty-or-not content offers no real evidence: either the subject is obviously enhanced or the claims are baseless speculation
The aesthetic bodybuilding community is crabs in a bucket full of drama, while powerlifting is a close-knit group pursuing a common goal
Set your own goals, do not set deadlines like five months, and do not wait for anyone, even him, to tell you what is achievable
The article's author is thin, does not train, and quit a gym for a month after an old man mocked his deadlift; his writing is projection
